four_slice_lengths.reason: dual meaning plus three post-construction mutation paths

entry_after.note: both still four cache lines; 192 not crossed

alternative_design.idea: five [*]T plus one shared installed flag, lengths from FrameLayout
alternative_design.cost: 107 length read sites must switch to derived values reached through frame.function

route_impact.p4_01b_premise: FrameLayout first because its 68 bytes need no consumer change
route_impact.status: falsified - crossing 192 bytes requires the FrameLayout-plus-installed-flag design, whose change surface is the same order as PlainEntry, so the two cannot be attributed separately

options.A: land only the 16 safe bytes (Stack memory/policy from Machine/runtime); Entry 256 -> 240, no line crossed, expected time gain near zero, ship as refactor not perf
options.B: treat Frame/Stack representation as one piece of work targeting 128 bytes, accept 107+ consumer changes and one broad semantic gate

recommended_next: before committing to B, run a cheap falsification of whether cache-line count is the bottleneck at all (e.g. induce a known line-count difference via the existing layout pad) rather than spending the change budget first
caveat: space is not time. P4-00 showed an ordinary return touches all four lines with hot fields spread across them; no existing evidence says 256 -> 181 or -> 128 converts into fib_rec time.
